properties.natural_language: Before preparing a transaction announcement via EDGE-PREPARE, the transaction must exist in the local mempool in a validated state with a valid hash, type, size, source address, and nonce
After preparing the announcement message, the NewPooledTransactionHashes message must contain all five fields: hash, type, size, source address, and nonce
After sending the announcement via EDGE-SENT, the 0x08 message must have been transmitted to all connected peers via the devp2p protocol
The announcement flow must follow strict ordering: TX-IN-LOCAL-POOL -> PREPARE -> ANNOUNCEMENT-READY -> SEND -> ANNOUNCEMENT-SENT, with no state skipping

Before receiving an announcement via EDGE-RECEIVE, the node must be in the awaiting-announcements state and the incoming 0x08 message must contain all required fields including DATA-TX-HASH, DATA-TX-TYPE, DATA-TX-SIZE, DATA-SENDER-ADDRESS, and DATA-TX-NONCE
After parsing the announcement, the metadata state must be marked as UNVERIFIED and must not be used for any security-critical decisions
After the pool interest check, the transaction must be classified as either interesting or not-interesting with no ambiguous intermediate state
If a transaction is deemed interesting, a GetPooledTransactions request must be issued to retrieve the full transaction data
Before metadata validation via EDGE-VALIDATE, the full transaction must have been successfully retrieved via GetPooledTransactions response
After metadata validation, all five announced fields (hash, type, size, address, nonce) must match the actual transaction or a mismatch state must be entered
After a metadata mismatch is detected, the announcing peer must be flagged as a protocol violator and its reputation reduced or connection terminated
Before processing untrusted data via EDGE-RECEIVE-UNTRUSTED, the system must recognize that announcement metadata from the external peer is unverified and potentially malicious
Untrusted announcement metadata must never be used for security decisions (access control, rate limiting by sender); it may only be used as an optimization hint for request prioritization
Filtering transactions based solely on unverified sender addresses constitutes censorship and must not prevent transaction propagation; filtering may only affect request priority ordering
The additional message size from B_20 address and nonce per transaction must not cause significant performance degradation or create a DoS vector
Before joining the sync committee subnet via EDGE-ASSIGNED-TO-JOIN, the validator must have been selected for a sync committee period approximately 256 epochs in advance
After joining the subnet, the validator must be subscribed to the correct gossip subnet for its sync committee duties before the 1/3 slot deadline
After producing a SyncCommitteeMessage, the message must contain a valid signature over the beacon block root and be published to the gossip subnet
After aggregation, the SyncCommitteeContribution must be published at approximately 2/3 through the slot and contain aggregated signatures from the subnet
The block proposer must select the best contribution per subnet (by highest signature count) and aggregate them into a SyncAggregate included in the beacon block
The sync committee lifecycle must follow strict temporal ordering: assignment -> subnet join -> message production (1/3 slot) -> aggregation check -> contribution (2/3 slot) -> block inclusion
Slot timing must enforce strict ordering: SLOT-START -> 1/3 mark (sync message deadline) -> 2/3 mark (contribution deadline) -> SLOT-END, with no phase overlap
Before publishing a SyncCommitteeMessage, the 1/3 slot mark must have been reached and the validator must have a synchronized clock
Before publishing a SyncCommitteeContribution, the 2/3 slot mark must have been reached and the aggregator must have collected messages from the subnet
Before computing aggregator selection proof, the validator must be a member of the current active sync committee
After computing the selection proof, the validator must be classified as either selected (~16 per subcommittee) or not selected, with no ambiguous state
All collected sync messages must reference beacon_block_root == block.parent_root to ensure consistency before aggregation
Before determining custody columns via EDGE-SLOT-TO-CUSTODY, a new slot must have started and the node must have a valid node ID for deterministic column assignment
Before sampling columns from peers via EDGE-START-SAMPLING, the node must have established a diverse peer set covering all required custody columns
After KZG proof verification, data availability must be confirmed if and only if sufficient valid column samples (>=50% columns reconstructable) are received
Custody column assignment must be deterministic based on node ID and must not be manipulable by attackers to concentrate custody of specific columns
Column sampling must use a cryptographically secure pseudorandom function so that an attacker cannot predict which columns will be sampled
Before blob transaction validation via EDGE-RECEIVE-BLOB-TX, the transaction must be received from the network with wrapper data including payload, blobs, commitments, and cell proofs

Blob transaction validation must follow strict sequential order: blob count check -> quantity match -> cell proof count -> KZG hash -> batch verify cell proofs, with any failure resulting in rejection
After blob count validation, the transaction must have at most 6 blobs or be rejected
The number of versioned hashes, blobs, and commitments must always be equal for a valid blob transaction
Before requesting missing columns from peers via EDGE-REQUEST-COLUMNS, the missing columns must be identified and peers custodying those columns must be known
After reconstruction, the full data matrix must be recoverable from at least 50% of columns via erasure coding, or reconstruction must fail explicitly
The reconstruction threshold of 50% columns is a fundamental cryptographic property and must be enforced regardless of network conditions
Before gossip distribution via EDGE-USER-CREATE, the user must provide valid blob transaction data with blobs and KZG commitments
After creating the transaction wrapper, the wrapper must use version=1 and contain blobs, commitments, and cell proofs in RLP format
Cell proof computation must be performed by the transaction sender (outsourced from block producer) and must be complete before gossip distribution
Before executing an I/O-intensive opcode via EDGE-OPCODE-DISPATCH, the EVM interpreter must dispatch the opcode with available gas information
After gas deduction for I/O operations, the increased gas costs must be applied (CALL: 40->700, BALANCE: 20->400, EXTCODESIZE: 20->700, SLOAD: 50->200)
Gas must always be deducted before executing the I/O operation; the operation must never execute if insufficient gas is available
Before executing a CALL operation via EDGE-CALL-START, the calling contract must provide target address, call value, call data, and requested gas
The 63/64 rule must always cap gas forwarded to child calls: available_gas = min(requested_gas, current_gas - current_gas/64), ensuring at least 1/64 gas remains with the caller
After child call execution completes, unused gas must be returned to the caller's gas counter
Before processing SELFDESTRUCT via EDGE-SELFDESTRUCT-OPCODE, the beneficiary address must be provided from the contract code
After SELFDESTRUCT, the contract balance must be transferred to the beneficiary and the contract must be marked for deletion at end of transaction
SELFDESTRUCT base gas cost must be 5000, with an additional 25000 gas charged if the beneficiary is a new account, preventing DoS via mass destructions
Before calldata gas calculation via EDGE-TX-SUBMIT, the transaction must be submitted with calldata bytes from an external submitter
Zero bytes must always cost 4 gas and non-zero bytes must always cost 16 gas (reduced from 68) per the EIP-2028 specification
Every byte in the calldata must be classified as either zero or non-zero with no unprocessed bytes remaining after iteration completes
Before gas limit validation via EDGE-RECEIVE-TX, the transaction must be received from an external submitter with a specified gas limit
Transaction gas limit must always be >= intrinsic gas (base cost + calldata gas at 16/4 per byte) for the transaction to be accepted
Before block propagation via EDGE-BLOCK-MINED, the block must be created by a miner potentially containing calldata-heavy transactions due to lower costs
Network propagation delay must satisfy the Sompolinsky-Zohar security bound: beta/lambda >= 1/(1 + D*lambda) to maintain chain security
Before EOF container validation, bytecode must be received and checked for the 0xEF00 magic prefix to determine format type
After magic byte check, bytecode must be classified as either EOF format (starts with 0xEF00) or legacy format, with no ambiguous classification
EOF validation must follow strict sequential order: magic check -> structure validation -> code validation, with any failure at any stage resulting in deployment rejection
Before stack flow analysis, the EOF code section must be loaded and ready for static analysis
Static stack validation must guarantee no stack underflow (popping from empty stack) and no stack overflow (exceeding 1024 items) across all execution paths
CALLF must push a return address to the internal return stack and RETF must pop the corresponding return address, maintaining strict LIFO ordering
JUMPF (tail call) must transfer execution to the target section without pushing a return address, distinguishing it from CALLF
Before EOF contract creation via EDGE-RECEIVE-CREATE, the deployer must submit a valid creation transaction with initcode and creation parameters
Both initcode and deployed code must pass EOF validation; failure at either stage results in creation failure with no contract deployed
After successful contract creation, the deployed contract must be valid EOF and accessible at the target address
Before fork activation evaluation via EDGE-NEW-BLOCK, a new block must be received or produced by a block producer with a valid block header
Fork activation must be deterministic based on block number: blocks below 7280000 use pre-fork rules, blocks at or above 7280000 use ProgPoW rules, with no ambiguous activation
The transition from pre-fork to post-fork state must be irreversible; once fork rules are activated, pre-fork rules cannot be re-applied for blocks at or above the threshold
Before block validation via EDGE-RECEIVE-BLOCK, the block must be received from a network peer with block data including the block number
Block validation must apply the correct ruleset based on block number: pre-fork PoW validation for blocks < 7280000 and ProgPoW validation for blocks >= 7280000
After PoW validation, the block must be classified as either valid or invalid with no ambiguous verification state
Before block proposal, the validator must be assigned to the current slot as block proposer
Before payload preparation via EDGE-TERMINAL-TO-PREPARE (pre-merge), the terminal PoW block must be identified via terminal total difficulty or override hash
After calling prepare_execution_payload, the execution engine must return a valid payload_id for later retrieval
After beacon block construction, the signed block must include the execution payload and be broadcast to the network
The block proposal pipeline must follow: slot assignment -> payload preparation -> payload building -> payload retrieval -> block construction -> block proposal, with no state skipping
Before block validation, the block must be received from a network peer for validation
Block validation must pass both beacon state transition and execution payload validation; failure in either results in the block being deemed invalid
Before calling engine_forkchoiceUpdated via EDGE-FC-TO-ENGINE-CALL, fork choice data including safe block hash, finalized block hash, and fee recipient must be available
After engine_forkchoiceUpdated call, the engine must either return SYNCING status or accept and return a payload_id; no other states are valid
The Engine API communication channel between consensus client and execution engine must be authenticated and local to prevent MITM payload injection
The fee recipient address must be correctly configured and not compromisable by external parties to prevent block reward theft
Before Osaka fork activation check, the system must be in pre-Osaka state and a block must trigger fork evaluation
After fork activation criteria are met, the system must transition to Osaka-active state and apply Osaka state transition rules
All previous fork rules (through Prague) must be correctly implemented and activated before Osaka fork can activate
Before block processing via EDGE-BLOCK-TO-VALIDATE, the block must be received from a network peer for processing under Osaka rules
Block processing must follow strict pipeline: structure validation -> transaction processing -> state trie update -> protocol requests, with each stage completing before the next begins
Before exception detection, the system must be actively processing a block under Osaka rules
After an exception is detected, the state must be fully rolled back to the pre-operation snapshot before error propagation
State rollback on exception must be atomic and complete; no partial state changes may persist after an exception is handled
Before the first memory write via EDGE-INIT-WRITE, memory must be in its initial empty state (empty bytearray)
Memory must be initialized as an empty bytearray at the start of each EVM execution context to prevent data leakage between transactions
After a memory write completes, the written data must be at the specified position and memory must remain in allocated state
After a memory read, the exact bytes at the specified position and size must be returned without modification
Before buffer read via EDGE-EXT-BUFFER-REQUEST, the opcode caller must provide valid buffer, offset, and size parameters
Buffer reads extending beyond buffer boundaries must always be zero-padded rather than causing an error, ensuring safe handling of out-of-bounds reads
Before a memory operation, gas must be calculated and charged for any memory expansion before the operation executes
Memory expansion gas must follow quadratic cost model and must be charged before write occurs; insufficient gas must result in out-of-gas exception with no state modification
Very large memory position values (U256) must be economically infeasible due to quadratic gas costs, providing a practical upper bound on memory usage
